title: The Heavy Chest
tagline: A 58-year-old with crushing chest pain. Every minute is myocardium.
objectives: Obtain and interpret a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of arrival.
Recognise inferior STEMI and look for right ventricular involvement.
Start early antiplatelet therapy and activate primary PCI without waiting for troponin.
Avoid treatments that harm a preload-dependent right ventricle.
Consider aortic dissection before giving antithrombotic therapy.

review.notes: AI-drafted teaching case built from current ESC 2023 and ACC/AHA guidance. Not yet reviewed by faculty. The uploaded textbooks were not available when this was drafted.

patient.name: Mr. Khalid
patient.background: Brought in by ambulance after collapsing onto a bench while walking.

lines: This is Mr. Khalid, 58. Central heavy chest pain that started about 40 minutes ago while he was walking.
He's sweaty and nauseated. Vomited once in the ambulance.
On scene: HR 98, BP 150 over 90, RR 20, sats 96% on air. GCS 15.
We didn't get a 12-lead in the vehicle — the machine was down. No drugs given. He's all yours, doc.

stateText.improving: He looks better — less pale, and says the dizziness has gone.
stateText.unchanged: He is still pale, sweaty and clutching his chest. Pain 8/10.
stateText.deteriorating: He is grey, clammy and says he feels faint.
stateText.critical: He is barely responding to voice, peripherally shut down.

actions.label: When did the pain start, and what were you doing?
actions.response: About forty minutes ago. I was walking to the mosque and it hit me — like a heavy weight. It hasn't eased since.

actions.label: Describe the pain. Does it spread anywhere?
actions.response: Heavy, crushing… like someone is sitting on my chest. It goes up into my jaw and down my left arm. Eight out of ten.

actions.label: Is it tearing? Does it go through to your back?
actions.response: No, not tearing, and not in my back. It's a pressure, right here in the middle.

actions.label: Any sweating, nausea or breathlessness?
actions.response: I'm soaked in sweat. I felt sick and vomited once. A little short of breath.

actions.label: Do you have any medical conditions?
actions.response: Diabetes for about ten years, and high blood pressure. I've never had heart problems.

actions.label: Which medicines do you take?
actions.response: Metformin and amlodipine. That's all.

actions.label: Have you taken sildenafil or tadalafil in the last 48 hours?
actions.response: No… never.

actions.label: Are you allergic to any medicines?
actions.response: No allergies that I know of.

actions.label: Do you smoke? Any heart disease in the family?
actions.response: Twenty cigarettes a day for thirty years. My brother had a heart attack at fifty.

actions.label: Any recent bleeding, surgery, stroke or stomach ulcer?
actions.response: No, nothing like that.

actions.label: General inspection
actions.response: Pale, diaphoretic and anxious, holding his hand over his sternum (Levine sign). Speaking in full sentences.

actions.label: Airway & breathing (A, B)
actions.response: Airway patent. RR 20, trachea central, equal air entry, chest clear with no crackles. SpO₂ 96% on room air.

actions.label: Circulation (C)
actions.response: HR 98 regular. Cool peripheries, capillary refill 3 s. JVP raised at about 6 cm, yet the lung fields are clear.

actions.label: Blood pressure in both arms and radial pulses
actions.response: Right arm 150/90, left arm 146/88. Radial pulses equal. No pulse deficit.

actions.label: Heart sounds
actions.response: S1 and S2 normal. No murmur (no new mitral regurgitation, no aortic regurgitation). No pericardial rub.

actions.label: Disability (D): GCS, pupils, glucose
actions.response: GCS 15. Pupils equal and reactive. Capillary glucose 9.2 mmol/L.

actions.label: Exposure (E): abdomen and legs
actions.response: Abdomen soft and non-tender, no pulsatile mass. Calves soft, no oedema. Temperature 36.8 °C.

actions.label: Attach cardiac monitor and defibrillator pads
actions.response: Monitor on, pads applied. Sinus rhythm on the screen.

actions.label: IV cannula (18G) and draw bloods
actions.response: 18G cannula in the right antecubital fossa. Bloods drawn and labelled.

actions.label: Aspirin 300 mg, chewed
actions.response: Aspirin 300 mg given to chew.

actions.label: Oxygen 15 L/min via non-rebreather mask
actions.response: Mask on. SpO₂ rises from 96% to 100%.

actions.label: GTN 400 mcg sublingual
actions.response: GTN spray given under the tongue.

actions.label: 0.9% saline 250 mL IV bolus
actions.response: 250 mL bolus running in.

actions.label: Morphine 2.5 mg IV
actions.response: Morphine 2.5 mg IV given.

actions.label: P2Y12 inhibitor load (per local primary PCI protocol)
actions.response: Given as per the cath lab's protocol. Note: pre-treatment practice differs between centres — follow your local protocol.

actions.label: Unfractionated heparin IV bolus (per protocol)
actions.response: Heparin bolus given according to the weight-based protocol.

actions.label: Give fibrinolysis (tenecteplase)
actions.response: Nurse: “Tenecteplase given… though the cath lab here is open 24/7.”

actions.label: Call the ED senior to the bedside
actions.speaker: Nurse
actions.response: Dr. Sara, the ED registrar, is on her way: “Good call. Get an ECG now if you haven't.”

actions.label: 12-lead ECG
actions.response: ECG recorded.

result.text: Sinus rhythm, 98/min. ST elevation in II, III and aVF (greatest in III), with reciprocal ST depression in aVL and I. ST elevation in III greater than in II suggests a right coronary artery occlusion.

actions.label: Right-sided ECG (V4R)
actions.response: Right-sided leads recorded.

result.text: ST elevation of 1.5 mm in V4R: right ventricular involvement. This patient is preload-dependent — avoid nitrates, and use opioids and diuretics with great caution.
Raised. In STEMI, troponin confirms the diagnosis later — it must never delay reperfusion.

actions.label: Venous blood gas
actions.requiresText: Needs IV access / a blood sample first.

result.text: Normal heart size. Lung fields clear. Mediastinum not widened. No pneumothorax. (Report only — no image is attached to this case.)
No aortic dissection. Incidental note: the scan delayed the patient by about 40 minutes.
Mildly raised — non-specific, and not helpful here.

actions.label: Inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement
actions.response: Working diagnosis recorded: inferior STEMI with RV involvement.

actions.label: Inferior STEMI
actions.response: Working diagnosis recorded: inferior STEMI.

actions.label: Anterior STEMI
actions.response: Working diagnosis recorded: anterior STEMI.

actions.label: NSTEMI
actions.response: Working diagnosis recorded: NSTEMI.

actions.label: Acute aortic dissection
actions.response: Working diagnosis recorded: aortic dissection.

actions.label: Acute pericarditis
actions.response: Working diagnosis recorded: pericarditis.

actions.label: Activate the cath lab for primary PCI
actions.requiresText: You need an ECG diagnosis before activating the cath lab.
actions.response: Cardiology on-call accepts: “Bring him straight up. Team will be ready in about 20 minutes.”

actions.label: Hand over and transfer to the cath lab
actions.requiresText: The cath lab team isn't here yet.
actions.response: You give a structured SBAR handover and the team wheels him to the lab.

actions.label: Admit to CCU for observation (no reperfusion)
actions.response: Bed requested on the CCU.

events.speaker: Nurse
events.message: Doctor, shall I put him on the monitor and pads? He looks grey.

events.speaker: Nurse
events.message: Doctor! His BP has dropped to 82/50 since the GTN. He says he feels faint.

events.speaker: Nurse
events.message: BP is now 74/44 after the morphine — he's barely responding!

events.speaker: Nurse
events.message: BP is coming up with the fluid bolus — 104/66 now, and he says the dizziness is better.

events.speaker: Nurse
events.message: Aspirin's in. He's tolerated it fine.

events.speaker: Cath lab nurse
events.message: The cath lab team is here to collect Mr. Khalid.

events.speaker: Senior
events.message: It's been a while since that ECG. What's the plan for reperfusion?

endings.title: Fast and safe reperfusion
endings.text: The angiogram shows a proximal right coronary artery occlusion, which is stented. He was pain-free by the end of the procedure, with good right ventricular function.

endings.title: He reached the lab — in shock
endings.text: The RCA was opened, but he needed vasopressors and a longer ICU stay. Hypotension in RV infarction is often iatrogenic — and avoidable.

endings.title: Reperfused
endings.text: He received primary PCI to the right coronary artery. Look at the feedback to see where time or safety could have been better.

endings.title: No reperfusion
endings.text: On the CCU his pain continued. A repeat ECG an hour later prompted a delayed cath lab activation. Time is muscle: STEMI needs immediate reperfusion.

endings.title: The shift ended without a reperfusion decision
endings.text: An hour after arrival he still had no reperfusion plan. The incoming team activated the cath lab.

rubric.good: Monitor and defibrillator pads attached early.
rubric.missed: Attach a monitor and defibrillator pads in the first minutes — STEMI patients can develop VF without warning.
Complete a structured A–B–C–D assessment.
Characterise the pain: onset, nature and radiation.
Ask about sweating, nausea and breathlessness.
Establish cardiovascular risk factors and past history.
Always check allergies before giving drugs.

rubric.good: Secured IV access and sent bloods.
rubric.missed: Secure IV access early.
Listen to the heart — a new murmur may point to a mechanical complication.

rubric.good: Correct working diagnosis: inferior STEMI with RV involvement.
rubric.missed: The working diagnosis was inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement (ST↑ II, III, aVF; ST↑ in V4R).

rubric.good: Recognised inferior STEMI (but not the RV involvement).

rubric.missed: Before antithrombotics, screen for aortic dissection: tearing pain or pain into the back, a pulse or BP difference between arms, a widened mediastinum.

rubric.good: Recorded right-sided leads in an inferior STEMI.
rubric.missed: In every inferior STEMI, record right-sided leads (V4R). ST↑ ≥ 1 mm means RV involvement.
The 12-lead ECG should be done within 10 minutes of arrival for any chest pain.

rubric.good: Recorded a 12-lead ECG (but later than 10 minutes).
Sent a troponin (without waiting for it).
rubric.missed: Send a troponin — but never wait for it before activating reperfusion in STEMI.
Send baseline bloods, including renal function and coagulation, before PCI.

rubric.good: Portable CXR — reasonable, and it didn't delay reperfusion.

rubric.missed: The CT aortogram wasn't indicated without features of dissection, and it delayed reperfusion.
D-dimer has no role in a clear STEMI. It is non-specific and can mislead.
Give aspirin (e.g. 150–300 mg orally) as soon as ACS is suspected, unless contraindicated.
Give aspirin early — within the first few minutes.
Primary PCI is the preferred reperfusion strategy when it can be delivered promptly.

rubric.good: Activated the cath lab within 15 minutes of the diagnostic ECG.
rubric.missed: Activate the cath lab immediately after the diagnostic ECG. Every 10 minutes of delay costs myocardium.
Call for senior help early in a time-critical diagnosis.
Fibrinolysis is for when primary PCI can't be delivered in time. With an on-site cath lab it adds bleeding risk without benefit.
Admitting a STEMI without reperfusion is a major error.
Nitrates in RV infarction cause profound hypotension — the right ventricle is preload-dependent. Check V4R before giving nitrates in any inferior STEMI.

rubric.good: Checked allergies before the first drug.
rubric.missed: Check allergies before giving the first drug.
Routine oxygen isn't indicated in ACS when SpO₂ is ≥ 90%.
Morphine in a hypotensive patient worsened the shock.
The hypotension was never treated — in RV infarction, give cautious IV fluid boluses and reassess.
Reassess after every intervention.
After a fluid bolus, reassess the response.

rubric.good: Reassessed repeatedly while waiting for the cath lab.
rubric.missed: Keep reassessing a STEMI patient while you wait for transfer.

keyPoints: Record a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of arrival for chest pain.
Inferior STEMI = ST elevation in II, III and aVF. ST elevation in III greater than II, with reciprocal change in aVL, points to the right coronary artery.
In every inferior STEMI, record V4R. ST elevation ≥ 1 mm means RV involvement.
RV infarction is preload-dependent: avoid nitrates, be careful with opioids and diuretics, and treat hypotension with cautious IV fluid.
Don't wait for troponin — STEMI is an ECG diagnosis, and reperfusion is time-critical.
Primary PCI is preferred when it can be delivered promptly. Fibrinolysis is for when it can't.
pearls: Raised JVP with clear lungs and hypotension in an inferior MI = think RV infarct.
Before antithrombotics, take 30 seconds to screen for aortic dissection.
